title: U.S. House · Missouri's 4th District
area: West-central and mid-Missouri, including Columbia's outskirts, Raymore, Lebanon and rural counties stretching toward the Lake of the Ozarks.

context.text: The 4th District attracted the most candidates of any Missouri U.S. House race in 2026: ten total, including incumbent Mark Alford, two other Republicans and seven Democrats. Alford won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Heather Shelton and Scott Vera. Jordan Herrera won a seven-way Democratic primary. Thomas Holbrook advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary. KathleenMae Rogers is running as a write-in, no-party candidate.

candidates.name: Mark Alford

summary.text: Mark Alford is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 4th District, first elected in 2022. A Texas native and longtime television news anchor in Kansas City, he serves on the House Appropriations and Small Business committees and is seeking a third term.

background.text: Born October 4, 1963, in Baytown, Texas; graduated from Baytown Sterling High School in 1982.
According to Wikipedia, he studied government at the University of Texas at Austin but left without graduating.

Worked as a television reporter and anchor in Texas and Florida markets, including KPRC-TV in Houston, before joining WDAF-TV (Fox 4 News) in Kansas City in 1998; his congressional website says he anchored Kansas City's morning news show for 25 years.

Ballotpedia lists career experience as a team lead and realtor with ReeceNichols Real Estate and a team lead manager with VortexKC/Chartwell; KCUR describes him as a former small-business owner and news anchor.

Announced his candidacy for Congress on October 27, 2021, won the Republican primary on August 2, 2022, and won the November 2022 general election to succeed Rep. Vicky Hartzler; he took office January 3, 2023.

In the 118th Congress he was assigned to the Armed Services, Agriculture, and Small Business committees; in the 119th Congress he moved to the Appropriations Committee and continues on Small Business, where he chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee.
Won reelection in 2024; KCUR reports he won more than 71% of the vote in both 2022 and 2024 and has President Trump's endorsement for 2026.
According to his congressional website, he is married to Leslie and they have three grown children, and he has raised money for charities and served on boards and civic organizations.

priorities.text: Formed an agriculture advisory committee to guide his work on farm bill policy for Missouri's 4th District, which has over 95,000 farms.

Focuses on securing funding for military installations in the district, including Whiteman Air Force Base and Fort Leonard Wood; helped secure $50 million for privatized family housing at Fort Leonard Wood.
As a member of the House Small Business Committee, focuses on the added challenges rural small businesses face and introduced the SBA Rural Performance Report Act (H.R. 5265).

positions.summary: Says he supports Second Amendment rights and will continue working to keep them intact, opposing further restrictions.
positions.quote: As long as I am in Congress, I won’t stop fighting to ensure America’s 2nd Amendment rights stay intact.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), including the Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies subcommittee and the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies subcommittee (Vice Chair).
Chairs the Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations Subcommittee of the House Committee on Small Business in the 119th Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Alford has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. His official issues page links to individual topic pages (agriculture, national security, Second Amendment, small business, veterans); only the Second Amendment page directly addressed one of the 15 guide issue statements. candidates.name: Jordan Herrera
candidates.ballotNote: Won a seven-candidate August 4, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Jordan Herrera is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 4th District. A nearly 16-year U.S. Air Force veteran who later served as a Missouri Assistant Attorney General, he has not held public office; he is campaigning on lowering costs, healthcare, veterans' issues and national security.

background.text: Born in Scottsbluff, Nebraska; graduated from Sidney High School. In his Ballotpedia survey, he describes growing up amid instability and violence.
Served in the U.S. Air Force from 2006 to 2022, joining at nineteen according to his Ballotpedia survey; Ballotpedia lists Air Force awards in 2010, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2020 and 2021.
Describes leading healthcare teams across eight states during the COVID-19 pandemic and deploying overseas during his service.
Earned an associate degree from Air University (2008), a bachelor's degree from Park University (2020), and a law degree from Southwestern Law School in Los Angeles (2024).
After leaving the Air Force, served as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Missouri.

Originally filed to challenge Rep. Emanuel Cleaver in the 5th District Democratic primary, then ran in the 4th District after Missouri Republicans redrew the maps; KCUR reports he won about 30% in a crowded seven-person Democratic primary in August 2026.
Ballotpedia lists affiliations including Indivisible KC, Respect MO Voters, Boots to Business and the Veteran Treatment Courts in Johnson and Jackson counties.

priorities.text: Economic security: lowering everyday costs, expanding access to affordable housing, protecting healthcare and raising wages to keep up with cost of living.
National defense: says national security requires a modern, ready military that uses taxpayer dollars responsibly while supporting service members and veterans.
Freedom and privacy: says government should protect individual rights and personal privacy.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Thomas Holbrook
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary

summary.text: Thomas Holbrook is the Libertarian Party nominee for Missouri's 4th District. A federal government contractor and history graduate, he says his experience with bureaucracy motivated his run.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born March 9, 1983, at Williams Air Force Base in Arizona and moved to Missouri about a year later when his father, an Air Force member, was assigned to Whiteman Air Force Base; he was raised near Leeton, Missouri.
Graduated from the University of Central Missouri with a Bachelor of Science in History in May 2011.

Reports work experience in food service, retail, tax preparation and civilian contracting; BallotReady lists him as a cashier at Walmart (2006-2016), general clerk at PAE (2017-2022) and Brillient Corporation (2022-2024), and document imaging specialist at Iron Mountain (2024-present).
BallotReady lists him as a candidate for Missouri's 4th District in the 2024 primary and general elections as well as in 2026.
KCUR describes him as a federal government contractor who said he distrusts bureaucracy and wants to dismantle it.

candidates.ballotNote: Running as a write-in candidate with no party affiliation

summary.text: KathleenMae Rogers is a write-in candidate with no party affiliation for Missouri's 4th District. KCUR describes Rogers as a Marine Corps veteran running as an independent write-in.

background.text: KCUR describes Rogers as a Marine Corps veteran running as an independent write-in candidate; no campaign website, fundraising figures or further biographical details were found.
